title: 'Time traveller' claims he's stuck in 2055 and shows 'FIFA 34' and 'GTA 7'
excerpt: A self-styled 'time traveller' claims he’s trapped in 2055 and has posted 'proof' in the form of FIFA 34 and GTA 7 - but viewers say the boxes are fake
content:
• News
  • Latest News
  • Time Travel

A self-styled 'time traveller' claims he’s trapped in 2055 and has posted 'proof' in the form of FIFA 34 and GTA 7 - but viewers say the boxes are fake

12:48, 26 Oct 2026Updated 12:51, 26 Oct 2026

A “time traveller” has baffled the internet after showing the “ultimate proof” that he is stuck in 2055. In a new video, posted to his popular Whitemask2055 social media, the content creator shows two video games, seemingly from the future.

‌

‌

FIFA 34, with Erling Haaland on it's cover, and GTA 7 (Grand Theft Auto) were shown off in the video many are saying is fake. “These games prove that I am really in the future!) the social media star wrote in the caption.

‌

In the clip, he tells followers he tried to track down the long-awaited GTA 6, but insists it’s impossible because, in his timeline, the game is now “far too old” - claiming it was released more than 30 years ago.

‌

He takes it a step further by saying he needs to find a PlayStation 7 so he can actually load the discs and play them. Keeping with the bleak tone of his universe, he also jokes that online gaming won’t be much use because 98% of the population has disappeared, leaving him as the last survivor in deserted streets.

But eagle-eyed viewers think the “proof” doesn’t stack up. Commenters say that when you zoom in on the small print on the back of the boxes, you can spot real legal wording linked to older games from our era - including references to Bandai Namco, 2020 legal notices and even PlayStation 4.

Others also pointed out that EA’s football series dropped the FIFA name in favour of EA Sports FC, making a future “FIFA” title look like a glaring mistake. According to multiple reports, the “White Mask 2055” phenomenon is a viral hoax and a piece of online fiction created by the social media account @whitemask2055, also known as “The Future Traveller”.

‌

In the videos, the creator claims he’s trapped alone in France in the year 2055 after 98% of humanity has vanished. To sell the sci-fi storyline, he regularly drops in “futuristic” props and references.

Behind the scenes, the entire project is driven by staging and slick visuals rather than anything real.

‌

Fact-checkers including Snopes have said the creator has previously flagged the content himself with phrases like “fake situation” or “creative project” in captions.

The eerie footage of empty Paris landmarks - such as the Louvre appearing deserted or the Eiffel Tower with no crowds - is understood to be captured at very quiet hours, recycled from COVID lockdown-era scenes, or produced using visual effects to remove passers-by.

‌

Viewers have also pointed to the “future” accessories as another giveaway. Items like the GTA 7 and FIFA 34 game boxes, along with drinks bottles showing expiry dates in “April 2055”, are believed to be custom-made physical props or digital overlays added for effect.
